title: Long-term Db2 coupling & flexibility hardening — dialect seam, embedding versioning, distributed-safe consolidation
description:
Audit (2026-08-08) of the memory core's long-term evolvability (`src/agent_memory_sdk/repositories/base.py`, `db/connection.py`, `db/migrate.py`), done through the lens of how OpenAI Agents SDK Sessions, Google Vertex AI Memory Bank, Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK Memory tool, and the closest architectural peer (Oracle AI Agent Memory) each trade storage portability against governance depth. The full market comparison already lives in `project-management/ai-agent-platform-competitive-analysis.md`; this epic captures the resulting engineering action items rather than repeating that analysis.

Core finding: `BaseRepository` (base.py, 2028 lines) is a Db2 repository pattern, not a storage-agnostic one — Db2 SQL dialect and `ibm_db` driver quirks/workarounds are hardcoded directly inside the shared base class instead of isolated behind a seam. This is not itself wrong — Oracle AI Agent Memory made the same converged-substrate trade, and SQL-enforced scoping/governance is genuinely hard to get from a generic storage interface. But several of the workarounds inside `base.py` are Db2-*version*-specific, not Db2-*family*-specific, and none of them currently have a mechanism to detect "this Db2 fixpack fixed the underlying issue, retire the workaround":

- Vector param binding unsupported (`SQL0901N`) → vectors inlined as SQL string literals via `CAST('{vec}' AS VECTOR(...))` (base.py ~lines 46-60, 1002, 1313, 1776, 1794).
- `JSON_VALUE(col,path) = ?` segfaults the ibm_db C extension → all metadata-filter values inlined as escaped literals instead of bound params (base.py lines 291-343) — the escaping/coercion function is now a safety-critical component, not just a convenience.
- `VECTOR_SERIALIZE()` and `VECTOR_DISTANCE()` can't combine in one statement → two-step rank-then-fetch query (base.py ~1758-1812).
- Zero-vector rows cause `SQL0801N` (division by zero) in `VECTOR_DISTANCE` → filtered out of `ORDER BY` explicitly (base.py ~1769-1776).
- Partial/filtered indexes unsupported (`SQL0104N`) → the `WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL` predicate was dropped from all 5 TTL indexes, eroding index selectivity as tables grow instead of failing loudly.

This epic also converts three risk-register items (`project-management/design/11-risk-register.md`) into tracked work instead of leaving them as prose: RISK-1 (in-process-only consolidation throttle counter — incorrect under >1 replica), RISK-2 (embedding dimension baked into DDL at migration time — a provider/model switch is currently a breaking migration with no drift detection), and RISK-4/RISK-6 (hybrid-search Python-side ranking cap, and `ibm_db` clidriver install friction) — the latter two are scoped as "watch/instrument" items, not redesigns, per the explicit decision not to speculatively over-engineer a multi-backend abstraction before there's data showing it's needed.

Relationship to other epics: distinct from EPIC-24 (CI/benchmark workflow DRY-ing) — this epic is about the memory core's own long-term evolvability, not its test infrastructure. No file overlap. FLEX-4 (hybrid-search instrumentation) pairs naturally with EPIC-24/CIB-3's planned 500k-row container-Db2 spike — both touch corpus-scale behavior and could share findings.
